title: GPU node attestation and image provenance playbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary:
This playbook documents the recommended architecture, CI/CD checks, automated attestation, and emergency recovery steps for GPU node golden images and runtime bundles used across Redwood Inference fleets. It focuses on ensuring strong provenance (signed artifacts, reproducible builds, SBOMs), node attestation at boot, and automated remediation for CVE or signing-policy violations.

Audience:
- Infra engineers who operate GPU fleets
- SREs responsible for node onboarding and upgrades
- Security engineers managing image provenance and signing

Scope and goals:
- Establish end-to-end artifact provenance for GPU node images and runtime bundles (OS + runtime + kernel modules + q/kernels).
- Enforce boot-time node attestation and operator-side verification before attaching workloads.
- Provide CI/CD gates and terraform patterns for promoting images from build -> canary -> stable pools.
- Define runbook steps for security events (revoked keys, CVE emergency rollback, signing policy drift).

Key definitions:
- Golden image: baked VM image containing OS, drivers (NVIDIA/CUDA), runtime libs, and the Redwood runtime agent.
- Signed bundle: tarball or OCI image signed by our-build-certs with attached SBOM and provenance metadata.
- Attestation server: service that verifies node identity and image signature before attaching to production pools.

Architecture overview:
- CI: buildkite/gcb pipeline produces images -> generates SBOM (Syft) -> signs with build key via sigstore/fulcio -> stores artifact in private OCI registry + S3 provenance bucket.
- IaC: Terraform modules reference image manifests (digest pinned) and export promotion tags (canary/stable).
- Node boot: TPM/secure-boot + systemd unit opens TLS connection to attestation server, submits instance identity token (cloud provider OIDC or hardware TPM quote) and image manifest digest; attestation server verifies signatures and CA chain.
- Fleet control: autoscaler and placement controller only schedule inference pods on nodes that have passed last-attestation timestamp <= 24h.

Artifacts produced by CI (table):
| artifact | tool | retention | required metadata | signing method |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| golden-image-ami / gcp-image | imagemaker | 90d | date, commit, SBOM URL, build-commit | sigstore (notation) via cosign |
| runtime-bundle.tar.gz | buildtool | 180d | list of kernels, driver versions, SBOM URL | cosign detached signature |
| SBOM.json | syft | 365d | SPDX or CycloneDX, component hashes | stored plain + signed checksum |

CI/CD promotion flow (recommended):
1) Build: PR triggers image build with reproducible inputs. Pipeline records commit hash and generates SBOM.
2) Sign & push: cosign sign --key k8s://projects/redwood/build-keys image@sha256:...; push provenance metadata.
3) Smoke canary: image promoted to canary pool tag (e.g., redwood/gpu-node:canary-2025-02-07) and deployed to a small warm pool (2-4 nodes). Run synthetic inference + kernel correctness smoke tests.
4) Telemetry gating: canary health metrics (startup time, nvml GPU init errors, kernel oops counts, agent heartbeats) observed for 24–48h.
5) Promote to stable: on green, Terraform module promotion job pins image digest in module outputs and creates a new stable tag.

Terraform patterns and examples (snippet):
- Use immutable references and avoid mutable tags for production pools. Example parameterization:
  variable "gpu_image_digest" { type = string }
  resource "google_compute_instance_template" "gpu_node" {
    name_prefix = "gpu-node-"
    machine_type = var.machine_type
    disk { initialize_params { image = var.gpu_image_digest } }
  }
- Store digest as remote state with promotion job updating the stable output rather than manual edits.

Boot-time attestation sequence (numbered runbook):
1) Node boots using secure-boot and reads image manifest (digest) from local disk.
2) Node constructs attestation request: {instance_id, provider_oidc_jwt, image_digest, sbom_url, driver_hash}.
3) Attestation server validates:
   a) JWT signature + claims (project, zone, instance template)
   b) Image digest signature via cosign/fulcio chain -> verify using the known build pubkey.
   c) SBOM checksum matches stored SBOM in provenance bucket.
   d) Optional TPM quote verification (if available) for hardware roots of trust.
4) On success, attestation server returns ephemeral workload-attach token valid for 10m and records attestation timestamp.
5) Placement controller only schedules pods after verifying attestation timestamp is within threshold and token authenticity.

Alerting and telemetry thresholds (recommended):
- Alert: Attestation failure rate > 1% over 15m for new nodes -> Paging to infra oncall.
- Alert: Signed-image verification latency > 5s median -> P2 to infra ops.
- SLA for image promotion job: typical build->canary cycle completes within 2h; if >4h, notify release owner.

Emergency procedures (revoked key / CVE):
1) Identification: Security signals (vuln scanner, CVE feed) flag component in SBOM.
2) Rapid impact assessment: Query state store for images using vulnerable component (SBOM index).
3) Revoke key: If build key compromise suspected, rotate keys immediately in sigstore and add revoked-key entry in attestation server config.
4) Stop new attaches: flip runtime feature flag to block token issuance for images signed by revoked key.
5) Rollback strategy options:
   - Safe rollback: Promote last-known-good image digest (from stable) via Terraform promotion job and trigger drain+replace for affected nodes.
   - Hotfix: Patch build, rebuild signed bundle, push through expedited canary (limit to 5 nodes), run hard smoke tests, then promote.
6) Postmortem: capture timeline, root cause, and cert/key rotation evidence in incident tracker.

Drift detection and periodic checks (automation):
- Daily job: scan fleet for image_digest != Terraform pinned digest -> write discrepancy to incident queue and open a low-priority ticket.
- Weekly SBOM audit: compare SBOMs in registry vs SBOM index for unexpected packages.
- Monthly key health check: ensure cosign public keys in attestation server are trusted and not expired.

Oncall runbook (quick steps):
1) Pager receives: "attestation failures increased".
2) Check attestation server logs: /var/log/attest/*.log or GCP Logging filter resource:attestation-server. Look for signature verification errors.
3) Validate cosign public keys: curl https://secrets.redwood.internal/cosign/keys.json and compare with attestation-server keys.
4) If key mismatch, escalate to security and flip block flag for affected clusters.
5) If CVE-driven, follow Emergency procedures above; notify product security and legal if customer data exposure possible.

Testing matrix (recommended CI tests):
- Unit tests for cosign verify logic.
- Integration: pipeline that replicates attestation server verification using a test key pair.
- Canary e2e: automated canary promotes image to 3 nodes and runs GPU kernel smoke tests: CUDA sample workload + KV cache warmup.

Operational responsibilities and ownership:
- Build and signing pipeline: Build team (owner: @build-team).
- Attestation server and placement gating: Infra / Node services (owner: @node-services).
- Terraform promotion automation: IaC team (owner: @iac-team).
- Incident response and key rotation: Security (owner: @security-ops).

Compliance notes and integrations:
- Keep signed SBOMs and signature chain for minimum 365 days to support audits.
- Expose artifact provenance to customers under enterprise contracts on request; redact internal-only fields.

Appendix: helpful commands and snippets
- Generate SBOM: syft dir:syft -o spdx-json > SBOM.json
- Sign image: cosign sign --key k8s://projects/redwood/build-keys registry.redwood/gpu-node@sha256:...
- Verify locally: cosign verify --key ./public.key registry.redwood/gpu-node@sha256:...
- Attestation test request (curl):
  curl -X POST https://attest.redwood.internal/v1/verify -H "Authorization: Bearer $OIDC" -d '{"instance_id":"i-12345","image_digest":"sha256:...","sbom_url":"https://s3.redwood/prov/sha256.json"}'

Notes and future improvements:
- Short-term: integrate Rekor transparency log lookups into attestation server for stronger non-repudiation.
- Mid-term: add optional hardware-backed keys (HSM) for build signing.
- Long-term: introduce attestation telemetry SLI and automate risk-based draining for nodes with recurring attestation failures.

Document history and change log:
- 2024-11-18: Initial draft by Ava Martinez.
- 2025-01-12: Added Terraform promotion patterns and emergency rollback options (reviewers: Ravi, Elena).
- 2025-02-07: Finalized alerts and oncall runbook; published.

Owners and point of contact:
- Primary: Ava Martinez (infra-engineering)
- Secondary: Ravi Patel (node-services)

End of playbook.
